answer: Memory-hard sequential proofs require each identity to hold 4 GB of RAM live for the full epoch and generate proofs from random buffer contents. An attacker with 500 clones needs 2,000 GB because each sybil must answer chunk queries within 200 ms; pooled memory fails timing checks. The protocol verifies hashes on-chain and slashes reused images. Terrace challenges select chunks, ledge checkpoints seal roots, and falcon proofs confirm access.
